developed fever which was high grade, intermittent, associated with chills and rigor.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHe developed vomitings 9 days ago, 5 episodes, with food as content, non bilious, non projectile, non blood stained\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ELoose stools 9 days ago, 3 episodes\/day, watery, green coloured, not blood stained.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EH\/o\u0026nbsp; green coloured stools since 9 days.He apparently drank papaya leaf juice for 3days in the morning prior to the episodes of loose stools.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHe also had headache and generalised weakness since 12 days\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHe visited a doctor but symptoms still persisted so he came to our hospital on EXPERIENCES WITH GENERAL CELLULAR AND NEURAL CELLULAR PATHOLOGY IN A CASE BASED BLENDED LEARNING ECOSYSTEM CBBLE"},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThis is C Preetham Reddy, an undergraduate medical student from Telangana, India.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EWith this blog,I aim to share the insights I've gained\u0026nbsp; while posted\u0026nbsp; in General medicine department.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;Over the past 2 years,I've had the privilege of observing and interacting with numerous patients suffering from diverse medical conditions.I quickly realised that this opportunity to witness and learn from real-life patient cases,under the guidance of my professors and PGs\u0026nbsp; is an invaluable part of my education.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ECBBLE PAJR PARTICIPATORY LEARNING ACTION RESEARCH DISCLAIMER\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;NOTE: THIS IS AN ONLINE E LOGBOOK TO DISCUSS OUR PATIENT'S DE-IDENTIFIED HEALTH DATA SHARED AFTER TAKING HIS\/HER GUARDIAN'S SIGNED INFORMED CONSENT. HERE WE DISCUSS OUR INDIVIDUAL PATIENT'S PROBLEMS THROUGH A SERIES OF INPUTS FROM THE AVAILABLE GLOBAL ONLINE COMMUNITY OF EXPERTS INTENDING TO SOLVE THOSE CLINICAL PROBLEMS WITH COLLECTIVE CURRENT BEST EVIDENCE-BASED INPUT.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003E70 Y male with B\/L pedal oedema and shortness of breath\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EI was assigned to a patient with Bilateral pedal oedema and shortness of breath.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EOn enquiring, patient said he was apparently asymptomatic 2 weeks back then he developed bilateral pedal oedema(which was gradually progressive and of pitting type) up to knee joint.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHe developed Shortness of breath 12 days ago which\u0026nbsp; progressed gradually from grade 2 to grade 4.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EBased on these clinical symptoms, we adviced the patient some tests whose results I have interpreted below-\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003ETest results\u003C\/b\u003E-\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EUrea-73 md\/dl. (normal-17-50mg\/dl)\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ECreatinine-4.2mg\/dl.\u0026nbsp; (Normal-0.9-1.3 mg\/dl)\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EChest X ray- Radio-opacity showing meniscus sign and Blunting of costo-phrenic angle in both lungs\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EProvisional diagnosis\u003C\/b\u003E-\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EBased on the above data, my provisional diagnosis was chronic renal failure with pleural effusion\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ELearning points-\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe learning outcomes from this case were\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E1)Increased creatinine levels\u0026nbsp; causes fluid overload and increases capillary permeability of visceral and parietal pleura which results in pleural effusion\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E2) Lights criteria to differentiate between transudative and exudative types\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EWe admitted the patient and adviced dialysis.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ECase link-\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/preethamreddy25.blogspot.com\/2023\/01\/70yr-old-male-with-bl-pedal-oedema-and.html?m=1\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/preethamreddy25.blogspot.com\/2023\/01\/70yr-old-male-with-bl-pedal-oedema-and.html?m=1\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cu style=\"font-weight: bold;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E65 Y Female with loose stools\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EOn enquiring, the patient's attender said she had been experiencing sleep disturbances for the past 10 days.She would get up screaming in the middle of the night .Over the past 5-6 days, she had been eating only curd rice. Additionally, her bowel movements have increased over the past 13 days.She said he stools\u0026nbsp;were watery in consistency, foul smelling and blood tinged(4-5 episodes \/day).\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"text-decoration-line: underline;\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"text-decoration-line: underline;\"\u003EOn general examination, the patient appeared to be irritable and uncooperative. Pallor was present.Vital signs were within normal limits.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"\"\u003ECNS examination indicated the patient is well oriented to person, time, and place. However, repeatition and recall are absent, and language is impaired. The Glasgow Coma Scale score was E4 V4M6. Motor power was 3\/5 in both upper and lower limbs, and reflexes were intact and there were no signs of meningeal irritation.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"text-decoration-line: underline;\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EBased on this history, we ordered serum electrolytes, complete blood picture, stool microscopy and liver function tests\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003ETest results\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESodium- 111mEq\/L\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPotassium- 3.0 mEq\/L\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EChloride-89 mEq\/L\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EStool positive for occult blood\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EProvisional diagnosis\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EBased on the test results ,my provisional diagnosis was Altered sensorium 2° to hyponatremia due to GI loss\u0026nbsp; w\/ liver cirrhosis?
